public_rationale: Bloomberg's document-based report identifies Lingmeixin, a Beijing company distinct from Megaspeed, as the purchaser and owner of B300 servers. That supports the narrow factual claim that another Chinese firm acquired Blackwell hardware. Moonshot's denial matters for the alleged rental, but does not directly rebut the identified owner's purchase. The evidence does not establish illegal export or NVIDIA's knowledge.
limitations: Relies on reputable reporting about records rather than independently inspected contracts.
Does not validate the speaker's certainty or the surrounding allegations of illegality.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: It is blatantly obvious that Megaspeed is not the only Chinese (or otherwise sanctioned-nation) firm acquiring or buying NVIDIA's Blackwell chips.

statement.excerpt: And it’s also blatantly obvious that this isn’t the only Chinese (or otherwise sanctioned nation) firm acquiring or buying NVIDIA’s Blackwell chips.

our_interpretation: The factual core is that at least one Chinese or sanctioned-country firm besides Megaspeed has acquired Blackwell hardware.
Buying servers containing the chips qualifies. Merely discussing a purchase or accessing an unspecified cloud service does not.
The claim does not require a direct purchase from NVIDIA or proof that the acquisition was illegal.

I read the statement as an acquisition-status observation through the post date. Earlier completed acquisitions can establish that another firm has obtained the hardware; no starting date is supplied.
criteria.support_condition: Credible transaction records or reporting based on such records identify another qualifying firm that acquired Blackwell chips or servers containing them by the post date.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comprehensive reliable records establish that Megaspeed was the only qualifying acquirer, or establish that all identified additional acquisitions were fictitious or involved other chip generations.
